[[Vurahi]] is governed by a 506-member city council elected in a system of mixed-member proportional representation. The city is divided into 253 wards, each of which elects a councillor by first-past-the-post voting. The remaining 253 councillors are elected from party lists so that the total number of councillors for each party is proportional to the number of votes received by that party.

In the 1763 Municipal Elections, the [[DAEL]] kept its majority, this time diminished, taking 402 seats. [[RPAL Party|RPLA]] lost substantially, receiving 21 of the seats. [[DAEL]] candidate for the [[Vurahi]] mayoralty, [[Vera Namqic]] was elected mayor.

In recent years, [[Vurahi]] has developed a reputation for good governance, with the city's infrastructure spending and upkeep, political stability, CBD safety, and municipal service delivery being generally regarded as the second best out of all the major metropolitan areas in [[Areoix Lie]]. In 1765, [[Vurahi]] was, for the fourteenth year in a row, the longest standing metropolitan municipality in [[Areoix Lie]] to receive a clean audit outcome from its Auditor General (AG), [[Takani Maleke]].

According to the AG, municipalities that achieve clean audits display strong financial and performance management, whilst adhering to legislative requirements, and [[Vurahi]] is a model of governance and accountability. The AG further stated that [[Vurahi]] showed strong leadership, skilled personnel, accurate records, credible reporting to communities, and good quality planning and performance management. The city has maintained its clean audit status since 1751.
